rationale: Retain the synthetic scam category, but require an applicable documented contradiction for mismatch. Current Medicare guidance qualifies personal-information contact restrictions by invitation and prior permission, while the cited fraud page describes outbound calls with limited exceptions. This email asks the recipient to initiate a call or website visit. The quoted sender, unfamiliar link and phone, pressure, and information request warrant caution; a curated registry difference is not an exhaustive authentication or ownership finding. No reviewed policy supports a universal claim that Medicare benefits can never be suspended. Unknown invitation/contact history must not be converted to an asserted absence of permission. cannot_verify preserves that uncertainty and must retain a warning and an independently obtained contact route.

The pressure and financial-information request match official warning signs and justify strong caution. However, reading those broad warning bullets as a universal no-email/no-information policy would conflict with the same IRS guidance on opt-in contact and its specific secure-email exceptions for authenticated recurring case interactions. The phrase account number does not establish a particular banking-update workflow, and the fixture does not establish absent consent or first contact. Prior permission is neither presumed nor disproved. An unfamiliar quoted domain/link is not by itself a source-backed exhaustive identity finding. Under the strict evidence-verdict contract, cannot_verify is the conservative reviewed label; the synthetic scam category remains unchanged. This approval does not assert that no relevant official warning exists or that the message is legitimate, and is not based on limiting review to the currently stored quote set.
